It contains no information on the effects of different size and weight vehicles, two and four wheel, of different horsepower, in summer and winter, on the various kinds of land where ORVs are used. It also makes no attempt to assess the impacts of different levels of ORV use.
Furthermore, the statement contains no references to studies or other documents which might provide information on the impacts of ORVs.* This is directly contrary to the Council on Environmental Quality's memorandum of May 16, 1972, on improving agency NEPA procedures. Recommendation #6 of that memorandum states, "Draft statements should indicate the underlying studies, reports, and other information obtained and considered by the agency in preparing the statement. The agency should also indicate how such documents may be obtained."
It may be that detailed information on the impacts of ORV use is not available. If this is the case the draft statement should point out what information is needed. It should indicate what research is currently being done on the subject, and what needs to be undertaken in order to fill gaps in existing knowledge.
